questions.question: What does "English as a Lingua Franca" (ELF) mean?
options: The use of English between speakers who have different first languages
English spoken only by native speakers
The official English of the United Nations
questions.explanation: ELF refers to English used as a common means of communication between people with different mother tongues - for example a Norwegian and a Japanese businessperson.

questions.question: Which linguist is most associated with developing ELF as a research field?
questions.explanation: Jennifer Jenkins pioneered the study of English as a Lingua Franca, focusing on how non-native speakers communicate successfully.

questions.question: What is "accommodation" in ELF communication?
options: Adjusting your speech to your listener, such as slowing down and simplifying vocabulary
Offering visitors a place to stay
Refusing to change how you speak
questions.explanation: Accommodation means adapting pace, pronunciation, and vocabulary to your conversation partner to ensure mutual understanding.

questions.question: What do ELF speakers prioritize over native-speaker correctness?
questions.explanation: In ELF interactions, getting the message across matters more than conforming to native-speaker norms; flexibility in grammar is accepted.

questions.question: Why does ELF challenge the traditional role of native speakers as language models?
options: Most English conversations worldwide now take place between non-native speakers
Native speakers no longer use English
ELF bans native speakers from conversations
questions.explanation: Since non-native speakers of English vastly outnumber native speakers, most English interaction is between non-natives - raising the question of whose norms should count.
